Subject: Mutual Action Plan: performance benchmarking + concurrency tests

Hi Emma —

Great talking yesterday. Per our discussion, I’m attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a proposed performance benchmarking plan specific to your throughput/latency goals. High-level asks from your side: production-like concurrency (simulating peak checkouts), TTFT targets for short prompts, and burst tolerance during marketing spikes.

Top-level proposal (attached MAP_AcmePayments_v1.xlsx):
- Evaluation window: 2 weeks (Sep 8 - Sep 21)
- Benchmarks we will run: latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT, throughput (req/s & tokens/s), and concurrency burst vs steady-state behavior
- Concurrency matrix: [1, 8, 32, 128, 500] clients, with both short (10-30 tokens) and long (200-800 tokens) output scenarios
- Acceptance criteria: p95 TTFT <= 250ms (short prompts), sustained throughput >= 180 req/s at 128 concurrent clients for the short-prompt path; no >1% error rate during steady-state.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the target test windows and any internal blackout dates.
2) We provision a dedicated test pool and share the test harness and scripts.
3) Karthik will run the baseline tests and share raw results + CSV.
4) Iterate on rate-limit tuning and queueing policy (token-bucket / leaky-bucket), then run a final acceptance sweep.

Attaching the MAP and a short test-plan doc. If that looks good I’ll lock Sep 8 as the start and schedule a 30-min kickoff with your infra team.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer

- We care about TTFT because it drives perceived latency in our checkout flow — our internal SLA target is p95 TTFT <= 300ms.
- The team would like to include a test that injects increasing queue depth to observe queueing behavior and how fallback/priority routing kicks in.

Sep 8 works for a kickoff. Can you include someone who can discuss rate-limit knobs and fallback routing (model variant fallback) — the infra team will want to see how Redwood behaves when a pool saturates.

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: performance benchmarking + concurrency tests — preliminary results

Hi all —

We ran the planned test matrix yesterday on a dedicated test pool (4xA100-equivalent nodes, model: open-compat-slim-v1 quantizable). Summary of preliminary findings (see attached redwood_concurrency_results_20250910.csv for full traces):

1) Short prompts (12 tokens output):
- Steady-state @ 140 concurrent: sustained 195 req/s, p50 TTFT = 95 ms, p95 TTFT = 210 ms, p99 TTFT = 360 ms; error rate 0.4% (mostly transient 429 during short warm-ups)
- Burst @ 420 concurrent (30s): observed queue depth spike and backend backpressure; effective throughput peaked at 380 req/s for the burst window but p99 TTFT spiked to ~1.2s and 503-like errors hit ~1.8% without burst tuning

2) Long outputs (400 tokens):
- Steady-state @ 32 concurrent: sustained 38 req/s, median TTFT = 360 ms, p95 = 820 ms
- Burst behavior: long-output paths caused queueing to starve short-prompt path unless we enabled priority routing (short prompts get priority tokens/sec budgets).

3) Rate-limit and queue tuning recommendations (what we applied to get acceptable behavior):
- Token-bucket per-route with burst allowance (configured to allow 2x sustained for 20s) — reduced 503s during marketing bursts
- Dynamic priority: short-prompt route receives higher priority tokens/sec; moved long-output traffic to a throttled lane during bursts
- Auto-shed long-lived requests when tail latency exceeds threshold to protect throughput for short prompts

4) Acceptance fit vs Acme targets:
- Short-prompt p95 target <= 300ms: PASS for steady-state; FAIL for un-tuned burst runs (p95 exceeded). With rate-limit + priority config, burst p95 improved to ~250ms for short prompts and error rate fell <0.5%

Next steps:
- Final acceptance sweep with the recommended rate-limit and priority config (we propose Sep 12 morning)
- Share CSV traces + Grafana links and a short notes doc detailing exact knobs and how they map to Redwood Console settings

Attachments: redwood_concurrency_results_20250910.csv, test-plan-parameters.md

—Karthik
Lead Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
